+    have been added.
+
+    .. code-block:: python
+
+      size = 4  # number of spatial orbitals
+

+
+      empty = ElectronicDensity.empty(size, include_rdm2=True)
body:
Since the API has num_spatial_orbitals as the name, not size, would it not be a little more straightforward to do this
```
num_spatial_orbitals = 4

empty = ElectronicDensity.empty(num_spatial_orbitals, include_rdm2=True)
```
or even
```
empty = ElectronicDensity.empty(num_spatial_orbitals=4, include_rdm2=True)
```
It ties things more closely to the names and avoids dealing with the indirect (size), which needs a comment here to clarify what it is, where the actual parameter name in the first place captures that intrinsically.

body:
Good question :sweat_smile: I do not recall a good reason why I would have made `from_orbital_occupation` a `staticmethod`. Probably because it does not use `cls` (although it should use that instead of hard-coding the `ElectronicDensity` to allow subclassing)..
The reason `empty` and `identity` are `classmethod` is because I mirrored this from `SparsePauliOp.zero` and `.one`, resp.

Maybe we can change this to be `classmethod` and at the same time change `from_orbital_occupation` to be a `classmethod`, too? I'm not sure about deprecation-implications of the latter though.. :thinking:
